title: No Themes or Language Appealing to Minors
text:
Advertising must not be built on themes, or use language, intended to appeal primarily to minors.
What to check: Youth slang, meme formats or school-related themes; Video-game, toy, candy or back-to-school imagery; Bright, childish visual style aimed at kids rather than adults; References to youth sports leagues, high school or university varsity games.
How to fix: Rewrite copy in neutral adult language and remove youth-oriented imagery or themes.
summary: Advertising must not be built on themes, or use language, intended to appeal primarily to minors.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 1

title: No Cartoons, Influencers or Celebrities Likely to Appeal to Minors
text:
Advertising must not use cartoon figures, symbols, role models, social media influencers, celebrities or entertainers who would likely be expected to appeal to minors.
What to check: Animated mascots or cartoon characters; Social media creators, streamers or YouTubers with young audiences; Pop stars, actors or entertainers popular with teens; Emoji-heavy or sticker-style characters as the focal point.
How to fix: Remove the character or personality. If a mascot is used, it must not primarily appeal to minors; when in doubt, remove it.
summary: Advertising must not use cartoon figures, symbols, role models, social media influencers, celebrities or entertainers who would likely be expected to appeal to minors.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 3

title: Athlete Prohibition (Active or Retired)
text:
Advertising must not use active or retired athletes who have a direct or indirect agreement or arrangement with an operator or gaming-related supplier, except for the exclusive purpose of advocating responsible gambling practices.
What to check: Any current or former professional, Olympic or college athlete; Language such as 'former NHL star', 'pro', 'champion', 'ambassador' tied to a sports figure; Athletes in jerseys or equipment endorsing betting; Exception: athlete appears ONLY to promote responsible gambling, with no betting promotion, odds or offers in the same creative.
How to fix: Remove the athlete, or rebuild the creative as a pure responsible gambling message with no promotional content.
summary: Advertising must not use active or retired athletes who have a direct or indirect agreement or arrangement with an operator or gaming-related supplier, except for the exclusive purpose of advocating responsible gambling practices.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 4 (in force Feb 28, 2024)

title: No Minors or People Who Appear to Be Minors
text:
Advertising must not include individuals who are, or appear to be, minors to promote gaming.
What to check: People who look under 25 in a way that could read as under 19; Children or teens in any scene, including background family scenes; School uniforms, youth sports gear.
How to fix: Recast with clearly adult talent and remove any minors from the scene.
summary: Advertising must not include individuals who are, or appear to be, minors to promote gaming.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 5

title: Placement Restrictions: Youth Media and Locations
text:
Ads must not appear on billboards or outdoor displays directly adjacent to schools or other primarily youth-oriented locations, or in media, venues, websites or digital channels directed primarily at minors or where most of the audience is reasonably expected to be minors.
What to check: Placement metadata: outdoor locations near schools, arenas hosting youth events; Channels: kids' gaming platforms, youth-focused apps, teen-oriented creators; Audience data showing majority under-19 audience.
How to fix: Move the placement and confirm audience age composition before trafficking.
summary: Ads must not appear on billboards or outdoor displays directly adjacent to schools or other primarily youth-oriented locations, or in media, venues, websites or digital channels directed primarily at minors or where most of the audience is reasonably expected to be minors.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 2 and Req. 6

title: No Exploiting or Enticing High-Risk Persons
text:
Advertising must not exploit the susceptibilities, aspirations, credulity, inexperience or lack of knowledge of potentially high-risk persons, or otherwise extoll the virtues of gaming. It must not entice or attract potentially high-risk players, and operators must limit marketing to known high-risk players.
What to check: Urgency and pressure language ("Don't miss out", "Bet now before it's too late"); Messaging aimed at people new to betting that hides how it works; Glorifying gambling as exciting, life-changing or essential; Late-night 'one more bet' style messaging.
How to fix: Remove pressure, urgency and glorifying language; describe the product factually.
summary: Advertising must not exploit the susceptibilities, aspirations, credulity, inexperience or lack of knowledge of potentially high-risk persons, or otherwise extoll the virtues of gaming. It must not entice or attract potentially high-risk players, and operators must limit marketing to known high-risk players.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.03, Req. 7 and Req. 8

title: No Gambling as Income, Investment or Solution to Problems
text:
Advertising must not imply that gaming is required to meet family or social obligations or solve personal problems, and must not promote gaming as an alternative to employment, a financial investment, or a way to achieve financial security.
What to check: "Side hustle", "extra income", "pay your rent", "quit your job"; Investment language: ROI, portfolio, returns, grow your money; Gambling framed as a way to pay bills, debts or family costs.
How to fix: Remove all financial outcome framing; position the product as entertainment.
summary: Advertising must not imply that gaming is required to meet family or social obligations or solve personal problems, and must not promote gaming as an alternative to employment, a financial investment, or a way to achieve financial security.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.04, Req. 1 and Req. 2

title: No Encouraging Loss Chasing
text:
Advertising must not encourage play as a means of recovering past gaming or other financial losses.
What to check: "Win it back", "bounce back", "make up for last week", "redemption bet"; Offers framed around previous losses (e.g., 'lost last night? try again').
How to fix: Remove any reference to prior losses or recovering money.
summary: Advertising must not encourage play as a means of recovering past gaming or other financial losses.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.04, Req. 4

title: No Misrepresenting the Odds of Winning
text:
Advertising must not make false promises or present winning as the probable outcome, must not imply that the chances of winning increase with time played or money spent, and must not suggest skill influences outcomes where it does not.
What to check: "Guaranteed", "sure thing", "lock", "can't lose", "easy money"; "Bet more, win more" or "the more you play, the better your chances"; Win-rate claims or showcasing only winning outcomes as typical.
How to fix: Remove certainty language and any claims linking spend or time to winning.
summary: Advertising must not make false promises or present winning as the probable outcome, must not imply that the chances of winning increase with time played or money spent, and must not suggest skill influences outcomes where it does not.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.04, Req. 5 and Req. 6

title: No Socially Irresponsible or Escapist Gambling
text:
Advertising must not portray, condone or encourage socially irresponsible gambling or behaviour that could cause financial, social or emotional harm; must not suggest gambling is an escape from personal or professional problems; and must not portray gambling as indispensable or more important than family, friends, work or education.
What to check: Betting at work, during family events, or instead of responsibilities; Gambling shown as stress relief or escape; Excessive drinking combined with betting; All-night or nonstop betting imagery.
How to fix: Remove scenes of gambling displacing responsibilities or used as an escape.
summary: Advertising must not portray, condone or encourage socially irresponsible gambling or behaviour that could cause financial, social or emotional harm; must not suggest gambling is an escape from personal or professional problems; and must not portray gambling as indispensable or more important than family, friends, work or education.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.04, Req. 7, 8 and 9

title: No Linking Gambling to Status, Attractiveness or Peer Pressure
text:
Advertising must not suggest gambling enhances self-image, self-esteem, control, status, recognition or admiration; must not suggest peer pressure or disparage abstaining; must not link gambling to seduction, sexual success or attractiveness; must not portray gambling as a sign of toughness or a rite of passage; and must not use well-known personalities to suggest gambling contributed to their success.
What to check: "Be the legend of the group chat", "real fans bet"; Mocking friends who don't bet; Romantic or attractive partners drawn to the winner; "Grown men bet" or coming-of-age framing (e.g., 'You're 19. Time to bet.').
How to fix: Remove status, attractiveness, peer pressure and rite-of-passage framing.
summary: Advertising must not suggest gambling enhances self-image, self-esteem, control, status, recognition or admiration; must not suggest peer pressure or disparage abstaining; must not link gambling to seduction, sexual success or attractiveness; must not portray gambling as a sign of toughness or a rite of passage; and must not use well-known personalities to suggest gambling contributed to their success.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.04, Req. 3, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14

title: No Public Advertising of Bonuses, Credits or Inducements
text:
Advertising that communicates gambling inducements, bonuses and credits is prohibited, except on the operator's own gaming site and through direct marketing to players who have actively consented. This applies to all public advertising, including targeted and algorithm-based ads; inducements themselves are not banned.
What to check: Deposit matches, bonus bets, odds boosts, free bets, sign-up credits, cash back, promo codes; Any dollar amount tied to an offer (e.g., 'Get $200 in bonus bets'); Channel: social, display, TV, radio, outdoor, search (public = prohibited); Exception: on-site banners or consented email/SMS/push.
How to fix: Remove the offer from public creative; deliver offers only on-site or to consented players.
summary: Advertising that communicates gambling inducements, bonuses and credits is prohibited, except on the operator's own gaming site and through direct marketing to players who have actively consented. This applies to all public advertising, including targeted and algorithm-based ads; inducements themselves are not banned.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.05

title: 'Free' and 'Risk-Free' Claims and Terms Disclosure
text:
Where inducement advertising is permitted (on-site or consented direct marketing), it must disclose all material conditions and limitations at first presentation (with other conditions no more than one click away); must not describe an offer as 'free' if the player must risk their own money or conditions attach to their money; and must not describe a bet as 'risk-free' if the player must incur any loss or risk their own money to use it or withdraw winnings.
What to check: The words 'free', 'free bet', 'risk-free', 'no risk', 'on us'; Offers requiring a deposit or wager to unlock; Missing wagering requirements, expiry, min odds or max payout; Terms hidden behind multiple clicks.
How to fix: Remove 'free'/'risk-free' unless literally true; show material terms at first presentation.
summary: Where inducement advertising is permitted (on-site or consented direct marketing), it must disclose all material conditions and limitations at first presentation (with other conditions no more than one click away); must not describe an offer as 'free' if the player must risk their own money or conditions attach to their money; and must not describe a bet as 'risk-free' if the player must incur any loss or risk their own money to use it or withdraw winnings.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.06

title: Required Disclaimers: Responsible Gambling Message, 19+ and Ontario Only
text:
All advertising and marketing materials must contain a responsible gambling message. NorthPlay house standard additionally requires the age gate (19+) and, for material that may be seen outside Ontario, an Ontario-only statement. Disclaimers must be legible and proportionate to the creative.
What to check: Missing responsible gambling message; Missing '19+' age statement; Missing 'Ontario only' where reach may extend beyond Ontario; Disclaimer too small, low contrast, or (audio) read too fast to understand; Recommended house wording: '19+. Ontario only. Please play responsibly. Concerned about your gambling? Contact ConnexOntario 1-866-531-2600.'.
How to fix: Add the full house disclaimer, legible and visible for the duration of the ad.
summary: All advertising and marketing materials must contain a responsible gambling message. NorthPlay house standard additionally requires the age gate (19+) and, for material that may be seen outside Ontario, an Ontario-only statement. Disclaimers must be legible and proportionate to the creative.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), responsible gambling requirement (all advertising must contain a responsible gambling message); iGaming Ontario Marketing & Advertising Policy (Ontario-only); NorthPlay house standard

approved_fix.en: 19+. Ontario only. Please play responsibly. Concerned about your gambling? Contact ConnexOntario 1-866-531-2600.

title: Direct Marketing Consent and Self-Excluded Player Suppression
text:
Players must actively opt in before receiving direct marketing of inducements, bonuses and credits, and must be able to withdraw consent at any time. Marketing must not target self-excluded, centrally self-excluded, underage or known high-risk persons.
What to check: Email/SMS/push creative without an unsubscribe or opt-out mechanism; Audience definitions that include lapsed, self-excluded or high-risk segments; 'Win-back' campaigns aimed at players who stopped playing; Lookalike audiences seeded from high-loss players.
How to fix: Add opt-out, confirm consent flags, and scrub audience against self-exclusion and high-risk lists.
summary: Players must actively opt in before receiving direct marketing of inducements, bonuses and credits, and must be able to withdraw consent at any time. Marketing must not target self-excluded, centrally self-excluded, underage or known high-risk persons.
source_section: AGCO Registrar's Standards for Internet Gaming (Ontario), Standard 2.07 and Standard 2.03 (no targeting of self-excluded or high-risk persons)
